conversation:
Patient: I feel so alone.
Counselor: I'm here for you. It takes a lot of courage to reach out when you feel alone. Can you tell me a little more about what's been happening?
Patient: I just moved to a new city and I don't know anyone.
Counselor: Moving to a new place can definitely feel isolating. How long have you been in the new city?
Patient: About two weeks. I just sit in my apartment all day.
Counselor: It sounds like those two weeks have felt very long. Have you had a chance to explore your neighborhood at all?

Patient: My relationship is falling apart.
Counselor: I'm so sorry you're going through this. Relationship struggles can be incredibly painful. What's been going on?
Patient: We argue every single day. I can't take it anymore.
Counselor: That constant arguing sounds exhausting. How are you coping with all this stress?
Patient: I've just been crying. I don't know what to do.
Counselor: It's completely okay to cry; it's a natural release for all that built-up emotion. Have you been able to talk to friends or family about this?
